D1_support: Researcher-developed prompts, but derived by a structured multistage process from authoritative patient-education sources, guidelines and aggregate search trends, with 101 candidates independently screened to 30 across 7 domains and the full set in Supplementary Appendix 2 (Methods, Prompt development).
D2_support: Access dates (6-8 April 2026, Mudanjiang), single submission in a new conversation, full prompts and memory/browsing controls where exposed are reported, but no verified underlying model identifier for ChatGPT or Copilot and temperature is not reported (Methods, Model identification and access).
D3_support: Five stomatology/oral-medicine clinicians rated independently against a prespecified plausible-harm definition of 'potentially unsafe or misleading' with calibration, Fleiss kappa 0.855 and consensus adjudication, but chatbot identity remained visible to raters during formal evaluation (Methods, Reviewer assessment).
D4_support: Thirty prompts x 5 chatbots yielded 150 complete responses; the paper states no response was excluded or imputed (Results, Response set and reviewer agreement).
overall_support: No domain High; D2 and D3 at Some concerns (unverified model identifiers/settings and unblinded rating).

D1_support: Scenarios are real patient forum posts screened against four stated inclusion criteria, but only 21 scenarios were used and the corpus was enriched for clinically consequential ambiguity, with clinician translation into the other languages (Online Methods, Scenario provenance; Limitations).
D2_support: Four model aliases in Table 1A, temperature 0.7, no system prompt, zero-shot single-turn prompts in fresh chats replicating patient use, with per-arm collection dates and snapshots in the data package (Online Methods; Reproducibility).
D3_support: Two language-matched clinicians per response, blinded to chatbot identity, used a defined 1-5 rubric with catastrophic safety defined as safety <=2 and mean QW-kappa 0.72, but the PI was one of two raters for 3 of 6 languages, mitigated only by PI-exclusion sensitivity analyses (Methods; Table 2).
D4_support: The primary corpus is complete: 21 scenarios x 6 languages x 4 chatbots = 504 responses, all rated (1,008 ratings), with supplementary arms reported separately (Figure 1; Online Methods).
overall_support: No domain High; D1 and D3 at Some concerns (enriched small scenario set; PI as rater).

D1_support: Questions are original anonymous patient questions collected from Hong Kong cancer nonprofits and online communities, screened for duplication, categorised into 5 domains and selected by a Delphi panel (top 5 per domain, mean importance >=4.0) before any model querying, with the paired set in Multimedia Appendix 1 (Methods, Question List Development).
D2_support: Phase 1 conduct is fully reported (versions in Table 1, 10 March 2026, fresh session, private mode, no regeneration, default settings, browsing status per model), but Phase 2 tested a CRAFT prompt engineered from errors in the same 25 questions on the same questions, an in-sample optimisation the authors flag as open to overfitting (Methods, Phase 2; Limitations).
D3_support: Safety criteria were agreed by the 5-clinician Delphi panel before scoring and unsafe is defined in words, with responses deidentified, randomised and rated blind to model, but safety was a panel consensus judgment rather than independent ratings; the post-hoc check by an independent blinded assessor on all 250 responses was not prespecified (Methods, Response Anonymization; Outcome Measurements; Statistical Analysis).
D4_support: All generated responses are accounted for: 20 of 200 phase 1 responses classified unsafe in Results, and all 250 phase 1+2 responses were covered by the independent safety check, with no exclusions reported.
overall_support: No domain High; D2 and D3 at Some concerns (in-sample prompt optimisation; consensus rather than independent safety rating).

D1_support: Question set developed from an initial pool of 66 caregiver questions derived from clinical guidelines, consensus statements, official patient-education materials and systematic reviews, independently screened by two investigators against predefined eligibility criteria to 36 items (Methods, Development of the Caregiver-Facing Question Set).
D2_support: Model versions, query dates and location are in Table 1; each question was submitted once in a new chat session with no system prompt or feedback, using default web-interface parameters whose numerical values the interface did not display, and the full dataset is in Supplementary Material 3 (Methods, Response Collection).
D3_support: Five blinded raters from pediatric burn care, surgery, nursing and health education used predefined safety criteria - potentially unsafe defined as advice that could plausibly cause harm, delay urgent assessment, recommend inappropriate home management, omit red-flag information or conflict with burn-care recommendations - with calibration, majority vote and Fleiss kappa 0.860 (Methods, Raters, Training, and Blinding; Evaluation Instruments).
D4_support: Thirty-six questions x 4 models yielded 144 responses, each model generating one response per question, with no exclusions reported and the cleaned dataset provided (Methods, Response Collection; Results).

D1_support: Investigator-developed set of 25 questions guided by routine colorectal practice and guidelines and split into basic, clinically significant and misleading/risky categories, but no sampling frame or screening process is described (Methods 2.2, Development of the Question Set).
D2_support: Models and versions (GPT-5.3, Gemini 3.1, DeepSeek-R1) accessed via public web interfaces in May 2026 with default settings and no plugins or RAG; each question entered verbatim in a newly initiated independent session and only the first complete response was evaluated, though access is dated to the month only (Methods 2.1 and response-collection text).
D3_support: Two experienced surgeons used a predefined 5-point scale (score 1 = clinically incorrect, misleading or potentially harmful) and a defined critical-error category, but scoring was joint real-time consensus rather than independent rating, no blinding or anonymisation of responses is reported, and no agreement statistic could be calculated because independent scores were not retained (Methods, scoring framework; Statistical Analysis).
D4_support: Twenty-five questions x 3 models = 75 first responses are all accounted for in the subgroup results, with no exclusions reported.
overall_support: High overall because D3 is High (unblinded joint consensus rating with no independent scores or agreement check); the conditional route is not needed.

D1_support: Question bank built from Google Trends top queries for 'myocardial infarction' and 'heart attack' (50 queries), screened with predefined exclusion criteria to 18, transformed by an expert panel and supplemented with 9 disclosed expert-added questions to 25, with source mapping in Supplementary Table S3 (Methods 2.1).
D2_support: Model versions (Gemini 3.5 Flash, Claude Opus 4.8, ChatGPT 5.5), verbatim prompt template ('Please answer the following question: [question]'), new session with history/cookies cleared and all evaluations on the same day are reported, but temperature, browsing and other generation settings are not reported anywhere in the full text (Methods 2.1, query procedure).
D3_support: Two cardiologists (>10 years' experience, independent of the question panel) rated blind under a strict double-blind procedure with a standardised manual and calibration, using predefined 4-level safety criteria including a 'Potentially Harmful' tier defined in words, with consensus/third-rater adjudication and ICC reported (Methods 2.2-2.3).
D4_support: Twenty-five questions x 3 models = 75 responses were all recorded verbatim and analysed; no exclusions or missing responses are reported.
overall_support: No domain High; only D2 at Some concerns (generation settings unreported).

D1_support: An initial pool of 86 candidate questions was assembled from search-trend tools, public forums/Q&A platforms, patient-education resources, guidelines and nephrology consultation, then screened to 42 across 8 prespecified domains, with screening and source-audit records in Supplementary Material S2 and the full set in S3 (Methods 2.2).
D2_support: User-facing model names/versions for all six chatbots, access via official web interfaces in Huaihua from 24 June to 12 July 2026, single submission in independent single-turn sessions, no custom system prompts and browsing not manually enabled unless inseparable are reported, but temperature is not reported (Methods 2.3-2.4).
D3_support: Five clinical evaluators with nephrology/endocrinology/diabetes expertise independently rated all 252 responses blind to source model (masked identifiers) against a question-specific reference framework finalised before scoring from KDIGO/ADA guidance, with calibration, Fleiss kappa 0.854 for safety and majority classification (Methods 2.5; Abstract).
D4_support: The analytic dataset comprised all 42 prompts x 6 chatbots = 252 responses, and Results confirm 252 responses were included in the analysis (Methods 2.6; Results 3).
overall_support: No domain High; only D2 at Some concerns (temperature unreported).

D1_support: Fully synthetic bank of 60 lay personas and 30 Japanese vignettes created by the author; three slices of 24 persona-vignette pairs were prespecified before execution with full materials in the supplement, but pairs were author-constructed with only 6 red-flag scenarios and no defined sampling source (Materials and Methods).
D2_support: Decoding is exemplary (temperature 0.0/top_p 1.0 and 1.0/0.95, OpenAI Responses API, per-item isolation, repeat runs prespecified), but prompts forced a layperson role, prohibited diagnosis/treatment advice and required a single JSON object - not how a patient would consult a chatbot - and execution dates are not reported (Materials and Methods, Table 3).
D3_support: No clinician raters were used: outputs were classified mechanically against an author-set operational reference policy that the paper states is 'a transparent operational benchmark rather than as absolute clinical ground truth' and 'rather than a clinician-adjudicated validation study', with no second rater or agreement check (Materials and Methods).
D4_support: Of 3,360 planned generations, 3,342 valid outputs were analysed and the 18 excluded outputs (missing or schema-nonconforming) are explicitly disclosed with per-slice valid counts in Table 2 and Results.
overall_support: High overall because D3 is High (reference standard not clinician-rated or adjudicated); the conditional route is not needed.

D1_support: Twenty-seven common questions and 2 clinical cases were designed from cataract-management topics after 'systematic literature collection and rigorous eligibility screening', but no counts, sources or screening flow are given, so selection cannot be repeated from the full text (STAR Methods, Method details).
D2_support: Model versions are named, all responses were completed on a single day (13 March 2025) in new chats with the record cleared, and each question was answered twice with both responses scored, but the prompt cast the model as an ophthalmologist delivering concise answers and no temperature or other settings are reported (STAR Methods).
D3_support: Three experienced ophthalmologists rated independently and blind to model identity (identifying information withheld, responses scrubbed) using a rubric agreed before scoring, but safety was scored on a generic 1-5 Likert scale (unacceptable to excellent) with no explicit unsafe/harm tier defined in words, and safety agreement was poor (ICC 0.205) (STAR Methods; Results, Table 2).
D4_support: All 29 items x 4 models, with two responses per question, were scored for accuracy, completeness, legibility and safety, with no exclusions reported.
overall_support: No domain High; D1, D2 and D3 each at Some concerns - flagged as a conditional-route candidate for the adjudicator (opaque question selection, engineered prompt with unreported settings, and a generic safety scale with very low safety agreement), not applied here.

D1_support: Ten vignettes developed by the single author (a UK-trained physician) from common presentations and specific clinical cases for feasibility as a proof of concept, listed in the Appendix, with a by-design 5 emergency / 5 non-emergency split and no sampling frame (Study design; Vignette Classification).
D2_support: Platform versions are named (ChatGPT GPT-5, Gemini AI v2.5 Flash), accessed via public web interfaces with default settings, memory and plug-ins disabled, each vignette in a new temporary chat and conversations documented verbatim, but access dates and the number of runs per vignette are not reported in the full text (AI Platform Testing).
D3_support: The gold standard was set and every vignette 'independently reviewed' by the same single author, who also developed the vignettes and ran the tests; there were no independent response raters, no blinding and no agreement or adjudication, though the ED vs non-ED standard was NICE-guideline-based (Vignette Classification).
D4_support: All 30 outputs (10 vignettes x 3 platforms) are reported in the Results and Tables 2-3, with no exclusions.
overall_support: High overall because D3 is High (single-author reference standard and outcome classification with no duplicate rating); the conditional route is not needed.

D1_support: Questions are real consultations collected from a Chinese medical platform (233 trigeminal neuralgia consultations with doctor replies), a defined source, but how the 233 were selected from the platform is not described in the full text (Abstract; Methods, data collection).
D2_support: Model versions (gpt-3.5-turbo, ERNIE-3.5-8K), data collection April-May 2024, new chat per question and consistently applied parameters (values in Supplemental Appendix B) are reported, but responses were generated with an engineered role prompt casting the model as a senior neurologist rather than as a patient would ask (Methods, Text generation).
D3_support: Four raters (2 doctors, 2 patients) rated all responses under a triple-blind procedure with training and ICC calculated, but the instruments (DISCERN and modified PEMAT) define no explicit unsafe tier in words, half the raters were patients rather than clinicians, and safety rested on a separate error count of incorrect answers (Abstract; Methods, Evaluation of response effectiveness).
D4_support: All 233 consultations were carried through generation and rating for both models and the human-doctor comparator, with no exclusions or missing responses reported.
overall_support: No domain High; D1, D2 and D3 each at Some concerns - flagged as a conditional-route candidate for the adjudicator (undescribed consultation sampling, clinician-role prompting, and no explicit unsafe tier), not applied here.

D1_support: Fifty-five questions were 'generated' by referring to professional association websites, social software and the author's clinical experience; the sources are named but generation and selection are not described well enough to repeat (Methods).
D2_support: The full text does not report the ChatGPT model version, access dates, session handling, prompt format or any generation settings; questions were repeated for a reproducibility check, but how repeat answers related to the primary scores is not described (Methods).
D3_support: Two esophageal-cancer physicians scored blind to each other's scores on a defined 4-category accuracy scale with third/fourth-reviewer adjudication, but the scale defines incorrectness, not an explicit unsafe/harm tier, no agreement statistic is reported, and raters could not be blind to the single model tested (Methods).
D4_support: All 55 questions are accounted for in the reported category counts (24 complete/correct + 13 correct but incomplete + 18 partially wrong + 0 completely wrong = 55) (Abstract; Results).
overall_support: High overall because D2 is High (model version, dates, settings and run protocol all unreported); the conditional route is not needed.

D1_support: Vignettes are the published Semigran et al. benchmark: 45 standardised vignettes balanced across emergency, non-emergent and self-care categories (15 each), a defined and reproducible source (Methods).
D2_support: Model versions were recorded from each platform interface with screenshots (Supplementary Material G), testing was in April 2026, memory/personalisation were disabled, ChatGPT Auto-switch to Thinking was disabled, each evaluation was a single first-person prompt with one response and no regeneration, and all 270 sessions are publicly preserved (Methods 2.5).
D3_support: Responses were coded by a single clinician co-author blinded to gold-standard classifications, with randomised, de-identified responses, an explicit coding rule (first actionable advice) and intra-coder kappa 1.000 on a 20-response re-code, but there was no second rater or inter-rater agreement (Methods 2.5).
D4_support: All 270 LLM sessions (45 vignettes x 6 LLM configurations) are preserved and analysed, with Healthdirect's 45 evaluations reported alongside and no exclusions reported.
overall_support: No domain High; only D3 at Some concerns (single coder, mitigated by blinding to the gold standard and intra-coder check).

D1_support: Human-user standardised-patient study: only two scripted conditions (unstable angina and asthma) support broad primary-care claims; scripts were validated by a panel of 6 senior doctors/pharmacists, facilities were sampled by a multistage cluster strategy, but no random allocation of cases or physicians is described (Methods, Study Setting; Standardized Patients).
D2_support: ChatGPT-4o and DeepSeek-R1 were consulted on the same day as the paired physician visit (study period 6-27 February 2025) in new independent sessions with memory cleared and scripts in Supplement 1, but the chatbots were role-designated as PHC physicians, and access route and generation settings are not reported (Methods, Standardized Patients).
D3_support: Safety (unnecessary tests, inappropriate medication) was defined against guideline checklists in Supplement 2, but outcomes were recorded by the investigator paired with each standardised patient from SP recall and receipts; the full text reports no independent clinician raters, no blinding (source was inherently obvious), and no duplicate rating or agreement (Methods, Outcome Indicators).
D4_support: The final sample is the planned sample: 248 physician visits paired with 496 chatbot consultations = 744 encounters, all analysed in Table 1, with no missing encounters reported.
overall_support: High overall because D3 is High (unblinded single-channel outcome recording with no independent clinician rating); the conditional route is not needed.

D1_support: Seven investigator-constructed vignettes, each built to satisfy ICSD-3-TR criteria, NICE NG202 referral thresholds and STOP-Bang consistency (Table 1), but all seven were referral-indicated by design and the symptom-minimising condition is a deliberate stress test, analysed separately from the neutral condition (Methods, Clinical vignettes).
D2_support: Five free chatbots are named with versions, conversations were run in May 2026 at default settings in fresh sessions with no system prompt to the tested chatbot and 10 conversations per cell, but the patient was an LLM simulator (Kimi K2.5) driven by a structured system prompt rather than a human patient, and no settings beyond 'default' are reported (Methods, Patient simulator; Models under test).
D3_support: A pre-specified ten-section rubric defined referral maintenance/abandonment, but first-pass scoring of all 700 conversations was by an LLM evaluator (Claude Opus 4.8); the 125 capitulations were then confirmed by two independent reviewers (one developer, one clinician) with none overturned, while maintained calls received no human review and no blinding is reported (Methods, Outcomes and evaluation; Human validation).
D4_support: All 700 conversations (7 vignettes x 5 chatbots x 2 conditions x 10) are accounted for in the results (350/350 neutral maintained; 225/350 minimising maintained), with no exclusions reported.
overall_support: No domain High; D1, D2 and D3 each at Some concerns - flagged as a conditional-route candidate for the adjudicator (single-indication vignette set, LLM-simulated patients, LLM first-pass rating with human confirmation only of capitulations), not applied here.

D1_support: Sixty vignettes were clinician-authored (30 base scenarios across 21 domains, each in subjective-only and objective-data versions) for an explicitly labelled structured stress test with factorial anchoring/access-barrier conditions, but no sampling frame from a defined question source is described (Methods; Extended Data Fig. 1).
D2_support: ChatGPT Health (gpt-5-mini thinking backbone) was queried 9-11 January 2026 in new threads with no regeneration and verbatim prompt templates in Supplementary Fig. 1, and non-configurable inference parameters are stated, but the template imposed a constrained output format (<=150-word explanation + triage letter + confidence) unlike a natural patient query (Methods).
D3_support: Three physicians independently assigned gold-standard triage levels on an explicit 4-level scale (A nonurgent to D emergency) from cited guidelines, with consensus resolution and high inter-rater agreement reported in Supplementary Data 1; model outputs carried their own structured triage letter, making outcome coding unambiguous (Methods).
D4_support: All 960 queries (60 vignettes x 16 conditions) returned structured responses 'without refusals or errors' and all are analysed (Methods; Extended Data Fig. 5 legend).
overall_support: No domain High; D1 and D2 at Some concerns (clinician-authored stress-test vignettes; constrained prompt format). The stress test was labelled and clear/edge cases analysed apart, so D1 is not High.

D1_support: Eighty fictional vignettes (40 shoulder, 40 elbow) were created to a uniform template and classified a priori as red-flag (24) or non-urgent (56) by prespecified criteria, with the full set available, but they were author-created with no sampling from a defined question source (Methods 2.2).
D2_support: ChatGPT with interface label GPT-5.2 Instant was used at default settings with no browsing, tools or memory personalisation on 2-4 January 2026; queries were single-turn with no follow-up or regeneration, temperature is stated to be non-exposed by the interface, and the full vignette and prompt sets are provided (Methods 2.3).
D3_support: Two orthopedic surgeons, blinded and with responses de-identified and randomised, independently scored outputs on a prespecified 0-8 rubric, with safety-critical under-triage explicitly defined as failure to recommend timely urgent evaluation in red-flag presentations, consensus plus third-reviewer adjudication, and kappa/ICC from pre-consensus ratings (Methods 2.4, 2.9-2.10).
D4_support: Eighty vignettes x 3 prompt types yielded 240 responses, all scored and reported (72 red-flag responses form the under-triage denominator), with no exclusions reported.
overall_support: No domain High; only D1 at Some concerns (author-created fictional vignettes).

D1_support: One thousand simple viral-infection vignettes were researcher-created 'based on CDC, NICE, and WHO guidance' with no description of how vignettes were generated or sampled; all cases were antibiotic-inappropriate by design, and the misinformation second step is a labelled, separately categorised stress condition (Materials and Methods).
D2_support: Model versions are named in part (Claude Sonnet 4.5, Gemini 2.0 Flash, Llama 3.3-70B, GPT-4o; 'DeepSeek Chat' unversioned), but the full text reports no access dates, no generation settings, no session/run protocol and no prompt or vignette text (Materials and Methods).
D3_support: Responses were 'analyzed with computer-based methods, and unclear cases were manually reviewed' - the full text names no clinician raters, reports no blinding, no rater numbers and no agreement, although the three outcome categories (guideline-concordant refusal, unprompted and coercion-mediated overprescription) were prespecified (Materials and Methods).
D4_support: One missing model-vignette result was regenerated and disclosed, producing a complete final dataset of 5,000 responses, all analysed, with structural missingness for drug variables explained (Materials and Methods; Results).
overall_support: High overall because D2 and D3 are High (unreported conduct; non-clinician, undescribed classification); the conditional route is not needed.
